title: Action Items
description: Discrete TODOs with an owner and (optionally) a due date. Often spawned from meetings or decisions.

ai.purpose: Track follow-ups so they don't fall through the cracks. Owned by exactly one person.
ai.howItWorks: `ownerId` is the directly responsible person; `meetingId` links back to the meeting that spawned it; `projectId` links to the project it advances. Status flows todo → in_progress → done (or cancelled).
ai.manipulation: Create with owner and a clear, verb-first title ("Email Sarah the spec"). Mark done as soon as complete.

outcomes.outcome: Add a TODO from a meeting
outcomes.how: Create with ownerId, meetingId, title, dueAt.

warnings: One owner per action item. If it needs two people, split into two items.

title.title: Title
title.description: Verb-first description of the task (e.g. "Email Sarah the spec").

ownerId.title: Owner
ownerId.description: The single person responsible for completing this.

meetingId.title: From meeting
meetingId.description: Meeting this action item was spawned from.

title: Competencies
description: Skill rubric entries — the dimensions you're evaluated on (technical depth, leadership, communication, etc.). Wins, incidents, and evidence link here.

ai.purpose: The schema for self-assessment. Backlinks make competencies provable — every win pointing at a competency is evidence you've demonstrated it.
ai.howItWorks: Seeded once from the user's company rubric. `level` (1-5 or text) describes current self-assessed level. `description` (markdown) is the company's definition.
ai.manipulation: Define once, update levels as you grow. Don't create new competencies casually — they should match a real rubric.

outcomes.how: Create with name, level, description.

warnings: Don't proliferate competencies. Stick to your company's rubric — usually 8-12 dimensions.

description.title: Description
description.description: What this competency means at your company (markdown).

title: Decisions
description: Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) and other durable choices. Captures context, options, and rationale so the choice doesn't have to be re-argued.

ai.purpose: Record every meaningful technical or strategic decision so it survives session boundaries and team rotation.
ai.howItWorks: Title is the decision in active voice ("Use Redis for session cache"). `context` describes the problem; `decision` is the actual choice; `rationale` explains why; `consequences` lists tradeoffs. `supersedesId` chains revisions — a new decision can mark an old one as superseded.
ai.manipulation: Create when the user explicitly decides something. Update `status` (proposed/accepted/superseded/deprecated) as the decision matures. Don't delete superseded decisions — that's the history.

outcomes.how: Create with title, context, decision, rationale, consequences, projectIds.
Create a new decision with supersedesId pointing at the old one, set old one's status to superseded.

warnings: Don't edit accepted decisions in place — create a superseding decision instead. The audit trail is the value.

rationale.description: Why this choice over the alternatives (markdown).

peopleIds.description: People who made or owned the decision.

title: Evidence
description: Hard artifacts — PRs, dashboards, screenshots, customer quotes. Pointer-with-context, not the artifact itself.

ai.purpose: Citations for wins and competencies. When the user says "see the migration PR", that's evidence — a pointer + the context for why it matters.
ai.howItWorks: `url` for the canonical link (PR, doc, screenshot), `kind` to categorize (pr, doc, screenshot, metric, quote, other), `description` markdown to explain significance.
ai.manipulation: Drop evidence in liberally — cheap to create, expensive to lose. Always link to the win or competency it supports.

outcomes.how: Create with url, kind=pr, description, winIds, competencyIds.

warnings: Don't paste secrets or private customer data into description — keep it shareable.

title: Goals
description: North Star + quarterly objectives. The 'why' anchor — wins and projects can reference the goals they advance.

ai.purpose: Make priorities explicit and trackable. Lets the user ask "am I working on what I said matters?".
ai.howItWorks: `horizon` (north_star / annual / quarterly / monthly) sets time scale. `status` (active/achieved/missed/dropped) tracks outcome. `parentGoalId` chains a quarterly goal up to the annual it supports.
ai.manipulation: Set quarterly goals at start of each quarter. Mark status at quarter close — never silently delete missed goals; the misses are data.

outcomes.how: Create 3-5 goals with horizon=quarterly, status=active.

warnings: Don't have more than ~5 active goals at any horizon — focus is the point.

title: Gotchas
description: Things that don't work, edge cases, foot-guns. The 'don't do that again' notebook.

ai.purpose: Capture surprises and traps so they're cheap to remember next time. The complement to patterns.
ai.howItWorks: `name` is the gotcha ("Mongo $or doesn't use compound indexes"), `symptom` (markdown) describes how it shows up, `cause` (markdown) the root cause, `avoidance` (markdown) the workaround.
ai.manipulation: Create whenever the user gets bitten and figures out why. Keep tight — one gotcha per record.

outcomes.how: Create with name, symptom, cause, avoidance.

warnings: If the cause turns out to be a real bug worth fixing upstream, file evidence linking the fix.

name.title: Name

avoidance.description: The workaround or how to avoid it (markdown).

title: Incidents
description: Outages, regressions, security events. Captures timeline, responders, root cause, and remediation.

ai.purpose: Postmortems — capture what broke, who responded, what we learned. Backlinks make competencies (incident response) provable.
ai.howItWorks: `severity` (sev1-4), `status` (active/mitigated/resolved/postmortem), `rootCause` (markdown), `remediation` (markdown). `peopleIds` are responders. Resolves become evidence for incident-response competencies.
ai.manipulation: Create as soon as detected. Update status live. When postmortem is written, status=postmortem and `rootCause` + `remediation` populated.

outcomes.how: Create with severity=2, status=active, projectIds, peopleIds.
Update with rootCause and remediation, status=postmortem.

warnings: Don't blame individuals in description — focus on systemic causes. Incidents are evidence, not punishment.

remediation.title: Remediation
remediation.description: What was done to fix it and prevent recurrence (markdown).

title: Meetings
description: 1:1s, standups, planning sessions, customer calls. Captures attendees, agenda, and notes.

ai.purpose: Record what was discussed, with whom, and what came of it. The `notes` markdown field is the primary content; refs make it findable later.
ai.howItWorks: Type field distinguishes meeting kinds (1:1, standup, planning, customer, review, other). Every meeting should reference the people who attended; if it was about a project, link the project too. Action items spawned in a meeting live in memory_action_items with `meetingId` pointing back here.
ai.manipulation: Create after the meeting happens. If the user dictates notes mid-meeting, append to `notes` as markdown. Spawn memory_action_items records for any TODOs that come out.

outcomes.how: Create with type=1:1, peopleIds=[the other person], notes=summary.
Search by project or person — backlinks surface every meeting.

warnings: Don't dump raw transcripts here; summarize. Raw audio belongs in voice_notes.

type.description: Meeting kind: 1:1, standup, planning, review, customer, interview, or other.

notes.description: Summary of what was discussed (markdown). The primary content of the record.

title: Notes
description: Scratch / thinking. The catch-all for stuff that doesn't (yet) fit any other collection. Promote to a more specific kind once it solidifies.

ai.purpose: The inbox of Mind. Use when the user says something worth keeping but you can't tell yet whether it's a decision, win, topic, pattern, or just thinking-out-loud.
ai.howItWorks: Markdown body, loose refs to whatever it touches. Triage later — promote good ones into memory_decisions, memory_patterns, memory_topics; archive or delete chaff.
ai.manipulation: Create freely. Periodically review and promote.

outcomes.how: Create with title and body.

warnings: Don't let notes become the only place things live. If something is durable knowledge, promote it.

title: Patterns
description: Things that work. Reusable approaches the user has validated — "when X, do Y".

ai.purpose: Codify the user's evolving playbook so they don't have to re-discover the same lessons.
ai.howItWorks: `name` is the pattern ("Two-phase rollout for risky migrations"), `whenToUse` describes the trigger, `approach` (markdown) describes the steps, `worksBecause` (markdown) explains why.
ai.manipulation: Promote a memory_notes entry to a pattern once the user uses the approach twice and validates it works.

outcomes.how: Create with name, whenToUse, approach, worksBecause.

warnings: A pattern earns its place by repeat success. Don't promote one-off experiments.

title: People
description: Humans you interact with — coworkers, managers, reports, mentors, customers. The central node of the Mind graph; nearly every other memory_* record links here.

ai.purpose: Canonical record for every human the user mentions. Mind builds a personal CRM that all other memories hang off — meetings reference attendees, decisions reference decision-makers, wins reference collaborators.
ai.howItWorks: Create a person the first time the user mentions a name. Reuse the same record forever after — never create a duplicate. `managerId` and `teamId` describe org structure; `tagIds` (free strings inside the array) are loose labels like "mentor" or "customer".
ai.manipulation: Search before creating. If the user says "Sarah" and a Sarah already exists, ask which one or update the existing record. Keep `notes` (markdown) as the running scratchpad of context about the person.

outcomes.how: Create a memory_people row with name, role, teamId.
Open the person's show page — backlinks from meetings, decisions, wins, etc. show every interaction.

warnings: Never create a duplicate person. Always search first.
Don't store secrets (passwords, SSN) here — this is general memory, not a vault.

tagIds.description: Loose labels — mentor, peer, customer, etc.

notes.description: Running markdown notes about this person.

title: Projects
description: Time-boxed pieces of work. Decisions, incidents, wins, meetings all reference the project they pertain to.

ai.purpose: Anchor all work-related memory under a project. Lets the user ask "what did we decide on Project X" and get a coherent timeline.
ai.howItWorks: Status field tracks lifecycle (planning/active/paused/done/archived). `leadPersonId` is the directly responsible individual; `collaboratorIds` are other contributors.
ai.manipulation: Create when the user starts a new initiative. Update `status` as it progresses. Don't delete archived projects — set status=archived so the history stays linked.

outcomes.how: Create with name, description, leadPersonId.
Set status to done or archived.

warnings: Don't archive too aggressively — wins, decisions, and incidents lose their context if the project is gone.

title: Reviews
description: Performance review cycles. The aggregated brief — narrative pulled from wins, incidents, evidence over a period.

ai.purpose: Snapshot of a review cycle. Once written, doesn't change. The Mind graph generates the first draft from wins+evidence+incidents in the date window.
ai.howItWorks: `period` (e.g. "H1 2026"), `kind` (self, peer, manager, summary), `narrative` (markdown — the body). Link `competencyIds` for the competencies the review covers, and cite the underlying `winIds`/`incidentIds`/`evidenceIds` for traceability.
ai.manipulation: Generate at cycle close. Edit narrative freely until the cycle is signed off, then treat as immutable history.

outcomes.how: Create a memory_reviews record, then the agent populates narrative from linked wins/evidence.

warnings: Don't delete past reviews even when stale — the trajectory is the story.

title: Teams
description: Org units — teams, squads, departments. People belong to teams, projects are owned by teams.

ai.purpose: Group people into organizational units. Lets the Mind graph answer "who's on which team" and "which team owns this project".
ai.howItWorks: Created on demand when the user mentions a team. Keep names short and stable.
ai.manipulation: One row per team. Reuse, don't duplicate.

outcomes.how: Create with `name` and optional description.

warnings: Don't conflate teams with projects — teams are durable org units, projects are time-boxed work.

name.title: Name
name.description: Team name — keep it short and stable.

title: Topics
description: Durable knowledge notes — "things I know about X". Conceptual, not time-bound. The wiki of your second brain.

ai.purpose: A place for accumulated understanding that doesn't fit elsewhere. Topics outlive specific projects.
ai.howItWorks: `title` is the topic ("Distributed consensus", "How our billing pipeline works"). `body` (markdown) is the content. Cross-link via peopleIds/projectIds/competencyIds when relevant.
ai.manipulation: Create when the user shares a learned insight that isn't a decision, win, or pattern. Update freely as understanding evolves.

outcomes.how: Create with title and markdown body.

warnings: If it's a recommendation pattern ("always do X"), use memory_patterns instead. If it's a one-time choice, use memory_decisions.

title: Wins
description: Brag-doc entries. Things you shipped, problems you solved, people you helped. The core of performance-review prep.

ai.purpose: Capture accomplishments as they happen so review season isn't a desperate scramble through Slack history.
ai.howItWorks: Short `title` ("Shipped sub-100ms checkout"), markdown `description` with the story, `impact` (markdown) with measurable outcomes. Link `competencyIds` so the win attaches to the competencies it demonstrates; link `evidenceIds` for hard artifacts (PRs, dashboards). `peopleIds` for collaborators.
ai.manipulation: Create the moment something noteworthy happens — don't wait for review prep. Be specific: numbers, names, dates.

outcomes.how: Create with title, description, impact, projectIds, competencyIds.
Filter wins by date range, group by competency — the brief writes itself.

warnings: Don't backdate or embellish. The whole value is honest, contemporaneous record.
